- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% for the next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) and prices are rising, model often underestimates the rally; adjust forecast upward by 3–8% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from the sentiment shift point, using 3–5 day lag to smooth transition.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 2–5% for days 25–30 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
